text:
aj: Quick heads-up — after the kernel-selector change last deploy, we're seeing a small-but-stable latency bump for short sequences under load. Not huge, but impacting p95 on small models.

emma: Saw that in the dashboard. p95 +18ms on 1-32 token requests when batch size stays <=4. p50 unchanged.

sahil: Link to profile? can you dump a perf trace or flamegraph? :mag:

aj: Pushed a short trace to the perf bucket: gs://redwood-perf/traces/1794007777/ — main difference is increased memcpy in the chosen kernel on short seqs.

yuri: Interesting — kernel selector is preferring the compact-matmul path now. Better throughput on long sequences but overhead on short ones due to copy+transpose.

aj: Yup. Hypothesis: selector cost heuristics prefer kernel that amortizes well at higher seq len, but admission + batching causes most requests to be sub-32 tokens so we pay the fixed cost.

emma: For continuous batching we should bias kernel selection based on the observed batch/seq distribution at admission time. i.e., if current queue shape is many short requests, pick low-overhead kernel even if theoretical throughput lower.

sahil: Agreed. Also we should tweak queue admission to avoid forming many tiny batches. Two levers: hold timeout and soft-admit based on token budget targets.

aj: Proposed quick experiment:
- token_budget_target = 512
- max_wait_ms = 6
- soft_reject_threshold = 88% of server token capacity

Try to prefer forming batches that reach closer to token_budget_target before forcing a flush.

yuri: I worry about tail-latency impact if we hold too long. max_wait_ms 6ms seems reasonable. Can we make hold dynamic: if kv cache hit rate > 80% then allow slightly higher wait because generation will be cheaper on GPU?

emma: Good call. KV cache hit reduces compute per token substantially. Proposed rule:
- if kv_hit_ratio >= 0.8 then max_wait_ms = 10 else 6

sahil: Also add queue-length cap for soft-reject to avoid head-of-line blocking: if queue_len > 200 requests, apply immediate soft 429 for new requests targeted to best-effort pool.

aj: Implementation note: soft reject vs hard reject. Soft should return a 429 with Retry-After and a header x-redwood-suggestion: try-dedicated or try-later. We should also emit a metric soft_reject_rate.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: rolling deploy to staging started for service=runtime-admission v=canary-2027-03-12

yuri: For kernel selection, adding a cheap heuristic: compute expected_total_tokens = max(current_queue_tokens, token_budget_target). If expected_total_tokens < 256 -> pick low-overhead kernel; else run selector as-is.

emma: Can we add an override flag on route config so customers can opt into latency-first vs throughput-first kernel profiles? Might be useful for PLG apps.

aj: Yes, route.conf could accept kernel_profile: [latency|throughput|auto]. Default auto uses live queue heuristics.

sahil: Quick perf target for the experiment: reduce p95 on short seqs by >=10ms without increasing p99 by >5%.

yuri: Also capture kv-cache-hit metric per batch and include it in the sample keys for the selector so we can A/B offline.

emma: I'll add to the console traces: per-batch {batch_tokens, batch_size, kv_hit_ratio, kernel_chosen, admission_delay_ms}

aj: Example config snippet I'm going to try on staging:

```
admission:
  token_budget_target: 512
  max_wait_ms: 6
  max_wait_ms_kv_hot: 10
  soft_reject_threshold_pct: 88
  queue_len_hard_cap: 200
  kernel_profile: auto
```

sahil: Sounds good. Also add metric for avg_admission_wait. We'll graph before/after.

yuri: I'll run a synthetic workload heavily skewed to 8-24 token requests to validate.

emma: If we see regressions, fallback plan: immediately disable new selector heuristic via feature-flag and roll back soft-admit changes.

aj: Staging run queued. Will post results in ~30m. tagging @yuri @sahil for follow-up.

sahil: quick note — ensure 429 responses include debug hint header for SDK to surface (eg, x-redwood-soft-reject-reason=token_budget)

aj: Agree. Also add sampling of request bodies for failed admissions to investigate hot routes.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary instances healthy (3/3) — cpu 45% gpu 38% mem 62%

yuri: First staging run results: p95 short-seq down 12ms, p99 flat, soft_reject_rate ~1.8% during burst window. kv-aware max_wait increased throughput by ~6% on those bursts.

emma: That's promising. Any adverse customer-facing 429s? SDK logs show automatic retry for most flows, but we should update docs to clarify Retry-After semantics.

aj: Next steps: run extended soak with mixed seq-length distribution, collect traces, and prepare rollouts with kill-switch flags. We'll keep default token_budget at 512 for now.

sahil: I'll add dashboards and alert if soft_reject_rate > 5% sustained or p99 increases by >10%.

emma: :thumbsup: Great work team. Thanks for quick iteration.

aj: Closing thread — follow up in #eng-monitoring once dashboards linked.
